79.title: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
79.summary: The application does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
79.why_it_matters: XSS vulnerabilities allow attackers to inject malicious scripts into web pages viewed by other users. This can lead to session hijacking, defacement, or theft of sensitive data.
basic_mitigations: Use output encoding/escaping for all user-supplied data
Use HTTP-only cookies for session management

89.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
89.summary: The application constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component.
89.why_it_matters: SQL injection allows attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands, potentially leading to unauthorized data access, data modification, or complete database compromise.
basic_mitigations: Use ORM frameworks with built-in protection

1021.title: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
1021.summary: The web application does not restrict or incorrectly restricts frame objects or UI layers that belong to another application or domain, which can lead to user confusion about which interface the user is interacting with.
1021.why_it_matters: Clickjacking attacks trick users into clicking on elements they cannot see, potentially leading to unauthorized actions or data exposure.
basic_mitigations: Set X-Frame-Options header to DENY or SAMEORIGIN
Use Content Security Policy (CSP) frame-ancestors directive

319.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
319.summary: The software transmits sensitive or security-critical data in cleartext in a communication channel that can be sniffed by unauthorized actors.
319.why_it_matters: Transmitting sensitive data over unencrypted channels allows attackers to intercept and read the information, leading to data breaches and privacy violations.
basic_mitigations: Use HTTPS/TLS for all sensitive communications
Never send credentials or sensitive data over HTTP

200.title: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
200.summary: The product exposes sensitive information to an actor that is not explicitly authorized to have access to that information.
200.why_it_matters: Information disclosure vulnerabilities can reveal sensitive data, system information, or implementation details that aid attackers in further exploitation.
basic_mitigations: Remove sensitive information from error messages
Audit and log access to sensitive information

352.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
352.summary: The web application does not, or can not, sufficiently verify that a well-formed, valid, consistent request was intentionally provided by the user who submitted the request.
352.why_it_matters: CSRF attacks force authenticated users to perform unwanted actions on web applications, potentially leading to unauthorized state changes or data modifications.

434.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
434.summary: The application allows the upload of a file with a dangerous type that can be automatically processed within the product's environment.
434.why_it_matters: Unrestricted file uploads can allow attackers to upload malicious files that are executed on the server, leading to remote code execution or system compromise.
basic_mitigations: Validate file types (check MIME type and extension)
Store uploaded files outside web root
Use whitelist of allowed file types
Rename uploaded files to prevent execution

601.title: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
601.summary: A web application accepts a user-controlled input that specifies a link to an external site, and uses that link in a Redirect.
601.why_it_matters: Open redirects can be used in phishing attacks to trick users into visiting malicious sites that appear to be legitimate, leading to credential theft or malware installation.
basic_mitigations: Validate redirect URLs against allowed domains

798.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
798.summary: The software contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key, which it uses for its own inbound authentication, outbound communication to external components, or encryption of internal data.
798.why_it_matters: Hard-coded credentials can be easily discovered and exploited, leading to unauthorized access and complete system compromise.
basic_mitigations: Use environment variables or secure vaults
Never commit credentials to source code

209.title: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
209.summary: The software generates an error message that includes sensitive information about its environment, users, or associated data.
209.why_it_matters: Error messages that leak sensitive information can reveal system details, user data, or implementation specifics that aid attackers in further exploitation.
basic_mitigations: Use generic error messages for users
Avoid exposing stack traces to users

311.title: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
311.summary: The software does not encrypt sensitive or critical information before storage or transmission.
311.why_it_matters: Unencrypted sensitive data can be easily accessed if storage or transmission channels are compromised, leading to data breaches and privacy violations.

326.title: Inadequate Encryption Strength
326.summary: The software stores or transmits sensitive data using an encryption scheme that is theoretically sound, but is not strong enough for the level of protection required.
326.why_it_matters: Weak encryption can be easily broken by attackers, rendering the protection ineffective and exposing sensitive data.

327.title: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
327.summary: The use of a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm is an unnecessary risk that may result in the exposure of sensitive information.
327.why_it_matters: Broken cryptographic algorithms can be easily compromised, allowing attackers to decrypt protected data or forge authentication tokens.
basic_mitigations: Avoid deprecated algorithms (MD5, SHA1, RC4, DES)

22.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
22.summary: The software uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the software does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
22.why_it_matters: Path traversal vulnerabilities allow attackers to access files and directories outside the intended directory, potentially leading to sensitive file disclosure or system compromise.

306.title: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
306.summary: The software does not perform any authentication for functionality that requires a provable user identity or consumes a significant amount of resources.
306.why_it_matters: Missing authentication allows unauthorized users to access critical functionality, potentially leading to data breaches, system compromise, or resource exhaustion.
basic_mitigations: Require authentication for all critical functions
Use multi-factor authentication for sensitive operations

307.title: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
307.summary: The software does not implement rate limiting or other restrictions on authentication attempts, allowing brute force attacks.
307.why_it_matters: Unrestricted authentication attempts allow attackers to brute force credentials, potentially leading to unauthorized access and account compromise.
basic_mitigations: Implement account lockout after failed attempts
Monitor and alert on suspicious patterns

502.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
502.summary: The application deserializes untrusted data without sufficient verification of the resulting data, potentially leading to remote code execution.
502.why_it_matters: Deserialization vulnerabilities can allow attackers to execute arbitrary code, leading to complete system compromise.

918.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
918.summary: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.
918.why_it_matters: SSRF vulnerabilities allow attackers to make requests from the server to internal resources or external systems, potentially leading to information disclosure or system compromise.

693.title: Protection Mechanism Failure
693.summary: The product does not use or incorrectly uses a protection mechanism that provides sufficient defense against directed attacks against the product.
693.why_it_matters: Missing or misconfigured security mechanisms leave applications vulnerable to attacks that could otherwise be prevented by proper security controls.

497.title: Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere
497.summary: The application does not properly prevent sensitive system-level information from being accessed by unauthorized actors.
497.why_it_matters: Exposure of system information can reveal implementation details, configuration, or infrastructure that aids attackers in planning further attacks.
basic_mitigations: Remove or obfuscate system information from responses
Disable verbose error messages in production

345.title: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
345.summary: The software does not sufficiently verify the origin or authenticity of data, allowing it to be spoofed or tampered with.
345.why_it_matters: Without proper verification, attackers can inject malicious data or impersonate legitimate sources, leading to various security breaches.
basic_mitigations: Use digital signatures for data verification
Use secure protocols with built-in authentication

829.title: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
829.summary: The software imports, requires, or includes executable functionality from a source that is outside of the intended control sphere.
829.why_it_matters: Including untrusted code can introduce malicious functionality or vulnerabilities into the application, leading to system compromise.
basic_mitigations: Use Subresource Integrity (SRI) for external scripts
Whitelist allowed sources in Content Security Policy

264.title: Permissions, Privileges, and Access Controls
264.summary: Weaknesses in this category are related to the management of permissions, privileges, and other security features that are used to perform access control.
264.why_it_matters: Improper access controls can allow unauthorized users to access sensitive functionality or data, leading to privilege escalation and data breaches.

598.title: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings
598.summary: The web application uses the GET method to process requests that contain sensitive information in the query string.
598.why_it_matters: GET requests with sensitive data can be logged in server logs, browser history, and referrer headers, leading to information disclosure.
basic_mitigations: Use POST method for sensitive data
Use request body for sensitive parameters

1004.title: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
1004.summary: The software uses a cookie to store sensitive information, but the cookie is not marked with the HttpOnly flag.
1004.why_it_matters: Without HttpOnly flag, cookies can be accessed by client-side JavaScript, making them vulnerable to XSS attacks and session hijacking.
basic_mitigations: Set HttpOnly flag on all sensitive cookies
Use Secure flag for HTTPS-only cookies

614.title: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
614.summary: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set, which could cause the user agent to send those cookies in plaintext over an HTTP session.
614.why_it_matters: Cookies without the Secure flag can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections, allowing attackers to intercept them.
basic_mitigations: Set Secure flag on all cookies in HTTPS applications
Never allow HTTP fallback for authenticated sessions

1275.title: Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute
1275.summary: The SameSite attribute for sensitive cookies is not set, or an insecure value is used.
1275.why_it_matters: Without proper SameSite attribute, cookies can be sent in cross-site requests, enabling CSRF attacks and cross-site information leakage.
basic_mitigations: Set SameSite=Strict or SameSite=Lax for sensitive cookies
Implement CSRF tokens as additional protection
Use HttpOnly and Secure flags together

201.title: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
201.summary: The code transmits data to another actor, but a portion of the data includes sensitive information that should not be accessible to that actor.
201.why_it_matters: Unintended transmission of sensitive data can lead to information disclosure, privacy violations, and compliance issues.

538.title: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory
538.summary: The product places sensitive information into files or directories that are accessible to actors who are allowed to have access to the files, but not to the sensitive information.
538.why_it_matters: Sensitive information in accessible files can be discovered by unauthorized users, leading to data breaches and system compromise.
basic_mitigations: Store sensitive files outside web root

1295.title: Debug Messages Revealing Unnecessary Information
1295.summary: The product fails to adequately prevent the revealing of unnecessary and potentially sensitive system information within debugging messages.
1295.why_it_matters: Debug messages in production can reveal implementation details, system information, and sensitive data that aid attackers.
basic_mitigations: Implement separate debug and production configs

548.title: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing
548.summary: A directory listing is inappropriately exposed, yielding potentially sensitive information to attackers.
548.why_it_matters: Directory listings can reveal file structure, sensitive files, and implementation details that aid attackers in planning further attacks.
basic_mitigations: Disable directory listing in web server config
Use index files in all directories
Remove unnecessary files from web root

550.title: Server-Generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
550.summary: Certain conditions, such as network failure, will cause a server error message to be displayed.
550.why_it_matters: Server error messages can reveal system information, database details, or implementation specifics that aid attackers.
basic_mitigations: Show generic error messages to users
Disable verbose error reporting in production
